byhyt: pa hyt (pa hyd) — what length; interrogative pa 'what' + hyt 'length', written as one word (Byhyt bynnac 'however long'); adverbial phrase, noun hyt m.; the b- and -y- are the spelling of pa hyt run together (uncertain how the b arose); no mutation of h-
fford: ffordd (ffordd) — road, way, journey; noun f. (ar y fford 'on the road'); ff written double, as against ford in 008; no mutation (ff does not soften), radical after the article y
chynnull: kynnull (cynnull) — to gather, collect; verbal noun (a chynnull eu cwn 'and gathering their dogs'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
boregueith: boregueith (modern form uncertain) — one morning, in the morning; adverbial compound of bore 'morning' + gweith 'time' (gu- = gw-), as treigylgweith 'one time'; no mutation (A boregueith)
wlaen: blaen (blaen) — front, fore part; noun m., in the phrase o ulaen 'in front of', where the b of blaen is fixedly softened (b>f); here o'e wlaen 'in front of them' with w written for the softened b (compare Vynt for wynt in 008); the possessive 'e 'their' is put inside the phrase
berth: perth (perth) — bush, thicket, hedge; noun f.; soft-mutated (p>b) after the feminine article ('r: y'r berth, a'r berth, o'r berth) and after the preposition y 'to' (y berth uechan 'to a little bush')
aant: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 pl. present 'they go' (yd aant y'r berth 'as they go to the bush'), the vivid present in past narrative; no mutation (vowel stem, after the particle yd)
cheginwrych: keginwrych (modern form uncertain) — bristling hackles, the raised bristles of a boar's back; noun m., apparently a compound with gwrych 'bristles' (first element uncertain); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a cheginwrych mawr aruthyr 'and great fearful hackles')
aruthyr: aruthr (aruthr) — dreadful, terrible, monstrous; adjective, after mawr (mawr aruthyr); no mutation
nessawn: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 1 pl. imperative 'let us draw near' (Nessawn parth a'r berth), in -wn; no mutation
nessaant: nessau (nesáu) — to draw near; 3 pl. present 'they draw near' (Pan nessaant), the vivid present in -ant; no mutation
uaed: baedd (baedd) — boar; noun m.; soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the presentative llyma (llyma uaed coed 'behold a boar of the wood')
coed: coed (coed) — wood, trees, forest; noun m., here (the old coet) as the genitive noun after baed: baed coed 'wild boar', literally 'boar of the wood'; no mutation
claerwynn: claerwyn (modern form uncertain) — bright white, shining white; adjective, a compound of claer 'bright' + gwynn 'white' (gw- lost in compounding); describes the masculine uaed; no mutation
hyder: hyder (hyder) — confidence, courage, heart; noun m. (o hyder y guyr 'heartened by the men', literally 'out of the confidence of the men'); no mutation after o
ruthraw: rhuthraw (rhuthro) — to rush, charge, attack; verbal noun (ruthraw idaw 'rushing at it'); r- writes rh-; any soft mutation (rh>r) cannot be told from the spelling
chilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chilyaw dalym 'and retreating a little way')
kyuarth: kyfarth (cyfarth) — barking, baying (of hounds at a beast); noun m., also the verbal noun 'to bark'; kyuarth a rodei 'baying it would give' (the dogs' baying round a boar at bay); radical, a fronted object before the particle a
gilyaw: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; verbal noun, soft-mutated (k>g) after heb 'without' (heb gilyaw yrdhunt 'without retreating from them')
yrdhunt: yrdhunt — conjugated preposition, 3 pl., 'from them' or 'before them'; written with dh for the /ð/ sound; perhaps a form of rac (cf. racdunt), but form and meaning uncertain; no mutation
ynghei: ynghei (lemma uncertain) — 3 sg. imperfect 'would draw close, would close in' (A phan ynghei y guyr 'and when the men would close in'); apparently from a verb related to yng 'narrow, close'; the meaning is taken from the context and is uncertain
kilyei: kilyaw (cilio) — to retreat, withdraw; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/it would retreat' (y kilyei eilweith 'it would retreat again'), habitual past; radical after the particle y
eilweith: eilweith (eilwaith) — a second time, again; adverb, eil 'second' + gweith 'time' (gu- = gw-, here lost in the compound); no mutation
torrei: torri (torri) — to break; 3 sg. imperfect 'would break' (y torrei gyuarth 'it would break bay', sense of the phrase uncertain); radical after the particle y
gyuarth: kyfarth (cyfarth) — barking, baying (of hounds); noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object directly after the inflected verb torrei (torrei gyuarth)
baed: baedd (baedd) — boar; noun m.; radical after the masculine article (y baed 'the boar')
kerdassant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they walked' (y kerdassant 'they went'); radical after the particle y following the fronted phrase yn ol y baed
gaer: kaer (caer) — fort, stronghold, fortified place; noun f.; soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article (y gaer, y'r gaer, yr gaer) and as the object after a verb (yny welynt gaer uawr 'until they saw a great fort')
newyd: newydd (newydd) — new, fresh; adjective (gueith newyd 'new work'); no mutation after a masculine noun
maen: maen (maen) — stone; noun m. (na maen na gueith 'neither stone nor work'); radical after na 'neither'
uuan: buan (buan) — swift, quick; adjective; soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after yn making it an adverb (yn uuan 'swiftly')
ryuedu: rhyfeddu (rhyfeddu) — to marvel, wonder; verbal noun (ryuedu a wnaethant 'they marvelled'); r- writes rh-; no visible mutation
chlywynt: klywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. imperfect 'they heard' (ny chlywynt 'they did not hear'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ny
gwney: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. present/future 'you do' (o gwney 'if you do'); radical gw- after o 'if' (o 'if' causes no mutation)
hynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m.; nasal-mutated (k>ngh) after uy 'my', written uyg hynghor (the g on the possessive and h on the noun spell the ngh, as in uyg kwn)
ey: mynet (mynd) — to go; 2 sg. present/future 'you will go' (nyt ey idi 'you will not go into it'), the suppletive stem e-; no mutation after the negative nyt
dodes: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 sg. preterite 'put' (a dodes hut ar y wlat 'who put an enchantment on the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would be unseen in the spelling
beris: peri (peri) — to cause, make (happen); 3 sg. preterite 'caused' (a beris bot y gaer yma 'who caused the fort to be here'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the relative a
madeuaf: madeu (maddau) — to forgive, let go, give up; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give up' (ny madeuaf i uyg kwn 'I will not give up my dogs'); written radical (m-) after ny, where the soft form uadeuaf would be expected
kwn: ci (ci) — dog; noun, plural cwn (written kwn with k); nasal-mutated (c>ngh) after uy 'my', written uyg kwn (= fy nghwn), the g on the possessive spelling the nasal
gaffei: caffael (cael) — to get, find; 3 sg. imperfect 'would get' (Pa gynghor bynnac a gaffei ef 'whatever counsel he would get'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a
mil: mil (mil) — animal, beast, living creature; noun m. (na mil 'nor any beast'); radical after na 'nor'; not the numeral 'thousand'
anhed: anned (annedd) — dwelling, habitation; noun f. (nac anhed 'nor a dwelling'), the old spelling with h; no mutation (vowel initial)
gymherued: kymherued (modern form uncertain) — middle, centre, midpoint; noun m., a compound of kyf- + perued 'middle'; soft-mutated (k>g) after the preposition am 'about' (am gymherued llawr y gaer 'about the middle of the floor of the fort')
fynnawn: ffynnawn (ffynnon) — spring, well, fountain; noun f.; f for ff; radical (ff does not mutate), after the article y (y fynnawn) and as subject of the list (fynnawn a gueith o uaen marmor 'a fountain with stonework of marble stone')
marmor: marmor (marmor) — marble; noun m. (maen marmor 'marble stone'), a borrowing from Latin; no mutation
chylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, ring, surround; noun m.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after y 'its' (yn y chylch 'round it', literally 'in its circle'), the possessive referring to the feminine fynnawn
lann: glann (glan) — bank, edge, shore; noun f.; g lost by soft mutation (gl>l) after the preposition ar (ar lann y fynnawn 'on the edge of the spring'); not llan 'church, enclosure'
cawg: cawg (cawg) — bowl, cup; noun (gender uncertain; also spelt cawc); radical (cawg uch benn llech 'a bowl above a slab')
llech: llech (llech) — flat stone, slab; noun f.; no mutation (uch benn llech 'above a slab'; wrth y llech 'to the slab')
chadwyneu: kadwyn (cadwyn) — chain; noun f., plural kadwyneu (-eu, modern cadwyni); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chadwyneu yn kyrchu yr awyr 'and chains rising into the air')
awyr: awyr (awyr) — air, sky; noun (yr awyr 'the air'); no mutation (vowel initial)
diben: diben (diben) — end, limit, top (of the chains); noun m. (a diben ny welei 'and an end he did not see'); radical, the object put before ny welei
gorawenu: gorawenu (modern form uncertain) — to rejoice greatly, be elated; verbal noun (gorawenu a wnaeth 'he rejoiced'), gor- 'over' + a verb from gwawen/llawen 'glad' (uncertain); no mutation
decket: tecket — fairness, beauty, fineness; noun m., the equative-form noun from tec 'fair' (-et); soft-mutated (t>d) after the preposition wrth (wrth decket yr eur 'at the fairness of the gold'); modern form uncertain
dahet: dahet — goodness, excellence; noun m., the equative form of da 'good' (-het) used as a noun, 'how good' (dahet gueith y cawc 'the goodness of the work of the bowl'); d- radical (after a 'and' d>dd is not seen in spelling); modern form uncertain
cawc: cawg (cawg) — bowl, cup; noun, spelt cawc with final c for g (y cawc 'the bowl'); radical after the article y; gender uncertain
ymeueil: ymauael (ymafael) — to take hold, grasp; 3 sg. present 'takes hold' (yd ymeueil a'r cawc 'as he takes hold of the bowl'), the vivid present, stem vowel a>e; no mutation
glynu: glynu (glynu) — to stick, cling, adhere; verbal noun (glynu y dwylaw wrth y cawc 'his hands sticking to the bowl'); no mutation
allei: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 3 sg. imperfect 'he/she could' (hyt na allei dywedut 'so that he could not speak'); g lost by soft mutation after the negative na
aros: aros (aros) — to wait, wait for, stay; verbal noun (A'e aros 'and waiting for him', 'e being 'him', the object); no mutation (vowel initial)
phrynhawn: prynhawn (prynhawn) — afternoon; noun m.; spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (A phrynhawn byrr 'and a short afternoon')
byrr: byr (byr) — short, brief; adjective, written byrr (prynhawn byrr 'a short afternoon', the day grown late); no mutation after a masculine noun
datcanu: datganu (datgan) — to declare, recount, relate; verbal noun (a'e datcanu oll 'and he recounted it all'), the 'e being the object 'it'; d- radical (soft d>dd would not show)
uuosti: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were' (buost) with the pronoun ti written on (buosti); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) as the verb of a sentence whose predicate is put first (ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti 'a bad companion you were')
golleisti: colli (colli) — to lose; 2 sg. preterite 'you lost' (colleist) with the pronoun ti written on; soft-mutated (c>g) after the relative a (a gedymdeith a golleisti 'a companion that you lost')
managassei: managu (a variant of mynegi, menegi; modern form uncertain) — to show, tell, declare; 3 sg. pluperfect 'he had shown' in -assei; radical after the particle y (y managassei ef 'that he had shown')
argel: argel (argel) — concealment, hiding, secrecy; noun m. (ny bu argel arnei 'there was no concealment on it', the gate not shut); no mutation (vowel initial)
deutroet: deudroed (deudroed) — two feet; noun m., the dual compound of deu 'two' + troet 'foot' (a'y deutroet 'and her two feet'); radical d- of deu
dwryf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt dwryf (twryf elsewhere in this part); soft-mutated (t>d) after the presentative llyma (llyma dwryf 'behold a noise')
chawat: kawat (cawod) — shower; noun f. (a chawat o nywl 'and a shower of mist'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and'
difflannu: diflannu (diflannu) — to vanish, disappear; verbal noun, written with ff (difflannu y gaer 'the fort vanishing'); no mutation
gloew: Proper name — Gloew (Gloyw in 008), second element of Gwyn Gloew, father of Cigfa; the adjective gloyw 'bright, shining'; radical after Gwyn
drygyruerth: drygyruerth (modern form uncertain) — lamentation, grief, wailing; noun, with drwc 'bad' as first element; fronted before a wnaeth (drygyruerth a wnaeth 'she made lamentation'); no mutation
marw: marw (marw) — to die, dying; verbal noun/noun 'death' (no'y marw 'than her dying'); no mutation of m- after 'y 'her'
drygyruerthy: drygyruerthu (modern form uncertain) — to lament, grieve; 2 sg. present 'you lament' (os … y drygyruerthy di 'if you lament'), from drygyruerth, in -y; radical after the particle y; lemma and form uncertain
uach: mach (mach) — surety, guarantor, pledge; noun m.; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after y (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'); whether y is 'his' or 'as' is uncertain
gywirach: kywir (cywir) — true, faithful, loyal; adjective, comparative gywirach 'truer, more faithful' (-ach); soft-mutated (k>g) after the soft-mutated noun gedymdeith (gedymdeith gywirach 'a more faithful companion'); cause of this mutation uncertain
uynho: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish, will; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) will' (tra uynho Duw it uot uelly 'while God wills it to be so for you'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after tra 'while'
et: et — uncertain: either the preverbal particle yd (spelt et, final t for d) after bei 'if', or the adverb et 'yet, still' (bei et uwni 'if I were yet/still ...'); no mutation seen on et itself
uwni: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I were' (bwn), with the pronoun i written on (bwn i); soft-mutated (b>u, = f) after the particle et following bei 'if'
gywirdeb: kywirdeb (cywirdeb) — faithfulness, loyalty, truthfulness; noun m., from kywir; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object directly after the inflected verb gadwn (mi a gadwn gywirdeb 'I would keep faithfulness')
cadwn: kadw (cadw) — to keep, hold, preserve; 1 sg. imperfect/conditional 'I would keep' (mi a'y cadwn 'I would keep it'); written radical, where soft mutation after the infixed object 'y 'it' would be expected
gey: caffael (cael) — to get, have, receive; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (titheu a gey y gedymdeithas 'you for your part will get the fellowship'), a short form beside keffy; soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
uynych: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may want' (a uynych y genhyf i 'which you may want from me'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the relative a
gallu: gallu (gallu) — power, ability; noun m. (herwyd uyg gallu i 'according to my power'); nasal-mutated (g>ng) after uy 'my', written uyg gallu with the g on the possessive
welho: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) see (fit)' (tra welho Duw 'while God sees fit'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after tra 'while'
dihirwch: dihirwch (dihirwch) — wretchedness, misery, worthlessness; noun m. (yn y dihirwch hwnn 'in this wretchedness'); no mutation after the article
goual: gofal (gofal) — care, anxiety, trouble; noun m., spelt goual with u for the /v/ sound; radical after the article ('r: a'r goual 'and the anxiety')
dalho: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may (God) repay' (Duw a dalho it 'may God repay you'), written with h before the ending (008 has dalo); soft-mutated (t>d) after the particle a
debywn: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think, expect; 1 sg. imperfect 'I would suppose' (a hynny a debywn i 'and that I would suppose'), written without the g (debygwn); soft-mutated (t>d) after the relative a
ehouyndre: ehofndra (modern form uncertain) — fearlessness, boldness, confidence; noun, from ehofn 'fearless'; final -e is the scribe's correction of -a (ehouyndra in the Red Book); no mutation after ac (vowel initial)
kyfle: kyfle (cyfle) — opportunity, fit place, convenient spot; noun m. (nyt kyfle yni trigyaw yma 'it is no fit place for us to stay here'); radical
trigyaw: trigyaw (trigo) — to stay, dwell, remain; verbal noun; no mutation
gollyssam: colli (colli) — to lose; 1 pl. preterite 'we lost' (Yn cwn a gollyssam 'our dogs we lost') in -yssam; soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
allwn: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 pl. present 'we can' (ymborth ny allwn 'we cannot feed ourselves'), ending -wn (as in gwnawn, kyrchwn); g lost by soft mutation after the negative ny; a 1 sg. imperfect would have the same ending, but the sense here is 'we'
loegyr: Proper name — Lloegr (Lloegyr beside Lloygyr), England; soft-mutated (ll>l) as the object directly after the verb (Kyrchwn Loegyr 'let us make for England')
hawssaf: hawdd (hawdd) — easy; superlative hawssaf 'easiest' (-af, modern hawsaf); adjective, as predicate (hawssaf yw in ymborth yno 'it is easiest for us to get food there'); no mutation
kerdyssant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, go; 3 pl. preterite in -yssant 'they walked' (Y gyt y kerdyssant 'together they went'); radical after the particle y following the fronted adverb
gymery: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. present/future 'you will take' (pa greft a gymery di 'what craft will you take'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
kymer: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 2 sg. imperative 'take!' (Kymer un lanweith 'take a clean one'); no mutation
lanweith: glanweith (modern form uncertain) — clean, neat, fine (of a craft); adjective, glan 'clean' + gweith 'work'; soft-mutated (g lost) after un with a feminine noun understood (kreft): un lanweith 'a clean one'
chymeraf: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 sg. present/future 'I will take' (ny chymeraf i 'I will not take'); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ny
crydyaeth: crydyaeth (cryddiaeth) — shoemaking, the shoemaker's trade; noun f., from crydd 'shoemaker'; radical after namyn 'except' (namyn crydyaeth)
hoff: hoff (hoff) — dear, pleasing, beloved; adjective, predicate (nyt hoff honno 'that (craft) is not pleasing'); no mutation
glanet: glan (glân) — clean, fair, fine, pure; equative degree 'as fine', used as a noun 'fineness' (glanet y wr 'fineness for a man', construction uncertain); ending -et; radical
kygynhilet: kynnil (cynnil) — thrifty, skilful, delicate, fine; equative degree kygynhilet 'as delicate/skilful' (ky- + kynnil + -et); radical; spelling and exact sense uncertain
thydi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. independent pronoun with the emphatic ending -di (tydi); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'as' (kyuurd a thydi 'of equal rank as you')
gvaegeu: gwaeg (gwaeg) — buckle, clasp; noun, plural gwaegeu (-eu); spelt gvaegeu with v for w; radical as the object of the verbal noun dechreu (dechreu gvaegeu 'beginning buckles')
waegeu: gwaeg (gwaeg) — buckle, clasp; noun, plural gwaegeu; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition o (o waegeu eureit 'of gilded buckles')
ouer: ofer (ofer) — vain, worthless, useless; adjective, u for the /v/ sound (ouer a man gueith 'worthless and petty work'); radical
man: man (mân) — small, fine, petty; adjective (man gueith 'small work'); radical after a 'and'
kynuigen: kenfigen (cenfigen) — envy, jealousy, spite; noun f., spelt kynuigen; radical (kynuigen a chynghoruyn 'envy and spite')
chynghoruyn: kynghoruyn (modern form uncertain) — envy, spite, malice; noun, spelt kynghoruyn (perhaps kynghoruynt); spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chynghoruyn)
rybudyeu: rhybud (rhybudd) — warning, notice; noun m., plural rybudyeu (-yeu); r writes rh; radical, after the verb doeth (yny doeth rybudyeu idaw 'until warnings came to him')
diodeuir: diodef (dioddef) — to suffer, bear, endure; 3 sg. impersonal present 'is suffered' in -ir, stem diodeu- (pam y diodeuir hynn 'why is this endured'); radical after the particle y
aem: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. imperfect 'we would go, we should go' (ni a aem 'we would go'); no mutation (vowel stem after a)
beich: baich (baich) — load, burden; noun m., spelt beich (dwyn beich o wenith 'carrying a load of wheat'); radical
wenith: gwenith (gwenith) — wheat; noun m.; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition o (beich o wenith 'a load of wheat') and as the object of a verb (na welsei dyn wenith 'no man had seen wheat')
gwelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun (no gwelet Arberth 'than seeing Arberth'); radical after no 'than'
tirogaeth: tiriogaeth (tiriogaeth) — territory, lands, domain; noun f., spelt tirogaeth (a'r tirogaeth 'and the territory'); no mutation after the article
kyneuinaw: kyneuinaw (cynefino) — to become accustomed, grow used (to), settle in; verbal noun (Dechreu a wnaeth kyneuinaw 'he began to grow used'); radical
pyscawt: pysgawt (pysgod) — fish; noun m., collective (hela pyscawt 'to hunt fish', to fish); radical after the verbal noun hela
llydnot: llwdn (llwdn) — young animal, beast; noun m., plural llydnot (-ot, modern llydnod); radical after a 'and' (ll- does not change)
gual: gwal (gwâl) — lair, bed, resting place of an animal; noun (ar eu gual 'in their lair'); gu- = gw-; no mutation after eu 'their'
ryuoryaw: ryuoryaw (lemma uncertain) — a rare verb, apparently 'to break and work the ground, to till', from the context (dechreu ryuoryaw 'beginning to till'); verbal noun; r- writes rh-; meaning uncertain
heu: hau (hau) — to sow; verbal noun, the Middle Welsh form heu (heu groft 'sowing a croft'); no mutation
groft: kroft (croft) — croft, small enclosed field (from English); noun f., written groft with t; soft-mutated (k>g) as the object of the verbal noun heu (heu groft 'sowing a croft') and after the feminine article (y groft 'the croft')
guenith: gwenith (gwenith) — wheat; noun m., gu- = gw-; radical after the masculine article (y guenith 'the wheat')
deir: tri (tri) — three; feminine form teir (tair), written deir; soft-mutated (t>d) after 'e 'his' (a'e deir grofd 'and his three crofts')
grofd: kroft (croft) — croft, small field; noun f., written grofd with d; soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article (y grofd, yr grofd), after the feminine numeral teir (deir grofd), after the feminine ordinal tryded, and as the object of a verbal noun (edrych grofd arall 'to look at another croft')
llwydaw: llwyddaw (llwyddo) — to prosper, thrive, flourish; verbal noun (yn llwydaw 'prospering'), progressive yn + verbal noun; no mutation of ll-
tegach: tec (teg) — fair, beautiful; comparative tegach 'fairer' (-ach); adjective (wenith tegach 'fairer wheat'); radical
amseroed: amser (amser) — time, season, period; noun m., plural amseroed (-oed); object of the verbal noun treulaw; radical (vowel initial)
kynhaeaf: kynhaeaf (cynhaeaf) — harvest, autumn; noun m.; radical after the masculine article (y kynhaeaf 'the harvest')
rofdeu: kroft (croft) — croft, small field; noun f., plural krofdeu (-eu), here written rofdeu with no initial letter (o'e rofdeu 'of his crofts'), as though the g of the soft-mutated grofdeu were lost after 'e 'his'; the spelling is odd but the word is clear
aeduet: aeduet (aeddfed) — ripe, mature; adjective (yn aeduet 'ripe'), predicative after yn; no mutation (vowel initial)
uedi: medi (medi) — to reap, harvest; verbal noun; soft-mutated (m>u, = f) directly after the verb uynhaf (mi a uynhaf uedi honn 'I will reap this one')
gefyn: kefyn (cefn) — back; noun m.; soft-mutated (k>g) after y 'his' (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', back again)
glas: glas (glas) — grey, blue, pale; adjective, of the pale light of dawn (E bore glas 'the grey morning'); no mutation after a masculine noun
dranoeth: trannoeth (trannoeth) — next day, the day after; adverb of time, soft-mutated (t>d) as an adverbial expression of time (E bore glas dranoeth 'at dawn next day')
medi: medi (medi) — to reap, harvest; verbal noun, radical after the verbal noun y uynnu and after uynhaf (y uynnu medi y grofd 'to want to reap the croft'; mi a uynhaf medi honn 'I will reap this one'), without the mutation seen in uedi
calaf: calaf (calaf) — stalks, straw, stubble; noun m., collective (y calaf yn llwm 'the stalks bare'); radical after the article
llwm: llwm (llwm) — bare, bleak, empty; adjective (yn llwm 'bare', predicative; y calaf llwm 'the bare straw', after its noun); no mutation of ll-
torri: torri (torri) — to break, cut off; verbal noun (daruot torri 'breaking having been done'); radical
dywyssen: tywyssen (tywysen) — ear of corn; noun f., plural tywys, tewys; soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (torri y dywyssen 'breaking the ear') and after yn y in the hard clause yn y dywyssen o'r keleuyn
keleuyn: keleuyn (celeuyn; modern form uncertain) — stalk, stem of a plant, the single of calaf; noun m. (o'r keleuyn 'from the stalk'); radical after the article
tewys: tywys (tywys) — ears of corn; plural/collective of tywyssen, spelt tewys (a'r tewys 'with the ears'); radical after the article; not the verb tywys 'to lead'
hollawl: hollawl (hollol) — whole, entire, complete; adjective (yn hollawl 'entirely'), adverbial yn; no mutation of h-
gorfen: gorffen (gorffen) — to finish, end, complete; verbal noun, written with a single f (yn gorfen uyn diua i 'finishing my ruin'); radical after the progressive yn
diua: diua (difa) — destruction, ruin, laying waste; noun m. (uyn diua i 'my destruction'); the nasal mutation of d- after uy 'my' is written as n on the possessive (uyn), the noun itself keeping d
orffen: gorffen (gorffen) — to finish, end; verbal noun; g lost by soft mutation after y 'its' (infixed object: yn y orffen 'finishing it')
diuawys: diua (difa) — to destroy, ruin, lay waste; 3 sg. preterite in -wys 'laid waste' (a diuawys y wlad 'who laid waste the land'); after the relative a, where d>dd would not show in the spelling
wlad: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country, realm; noun f., written wlad with d for t; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the feminine article y
wylaf: gwylat (gwylio) — to watch, keep watch; 1 sg. present/future 'I will watch' (ony wylaf i 'unless I watch'; mi a wylaf y grofd 'I will watch the croft'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after ony 'unless' and after the particle a
eliwlu: eliwlu (lemma uncertain) — a rare word, apparently 'host, vast multitude' (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the greatest host in the world of mice'); noun; meaning from the context and uncertain
lygot: llygot (llygod) — mice; plural of llygoden; noun; soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition o (o lygot 'of mice')
chyfrif: kyfrif (cyfrif) — counting, reckoning, number; noun m.; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyfrif na messur 'and count nor measure')
messur: mesur (mesur) — measure, measuring; noun m., written with ss (na messur 'nor measure'); radical after na
llygot: llygot (llygod) — mice; plural of llygoden; noun (y llygot 'the mice'); radical after the article
adan: adan (dan, 'under'; adan is the older form) — under, beneath; preposition (adan y grofd 'under the croft'); no mutation
drigyaw: dringaw (dringo) — to climb; verbal noun, apparently written drigyaw without the n (phob un yn drigyaw 'each one climbing'); radical after yn; spelling and reading somewhat uncertain
kyleuyn: keleuyn (celeuyn; modern form uncertain) — stalk, stem; noun m., spelt kyleuyn (ar hyt y kyleuyn 'along the stalk'); radical after the article
estwng: estwng (estwng) — to lower, bend down, bring down; verbal noun (yn y estwng genti 'bending it down, with her'); no mutation (vowel initial)
tywys: tywys (tywys) — ears of corn; plural/collective of tywyssen (a'r tywys 'and the ears'); radical after the article; not the verb tywys 'to lead'
wydyat: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 3 sg. imperfect 'he knew' (ni wydyat ef 'he did not know'), spelt wydyat beside wydat; g- lost by soft mutation (gw>w) after the negative ni
lygoden: llygoden (llygoden) — mouse; noun f., plural llygot; soft-mutated (ll>l) as the subject directly after the verb bei (ny bei lygoden 'there was not a mouse')
gymerynt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would take, they took' (a gymerynt eu hynt 'and they took their way'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
dicter: dicter (dicter) — anger, wrath; noun m. (rwng dicter a llit 'between anger and wrath'); radical
llit: llid (llid) — anger, wrath, rage; noun m., spelt llit with final t for d; radical after a 'and'
gwydbet: gwybed (gwybed) — gnats, midges; collective/plural noun, spelt gwydbet with an extra d (ar y gwydbet 'on the midges'); gu- = gw-; radical after the article
chytdremei: kytdremu (modern form uncertain) — to keep in sight, look steadily at; 3 sg. imperfect 'he could keep in sight' (ni chytdremei ef ar 'he could not keep his eyes on'), from kyt- + drem 'sight'; spirant-mutated (k>ch) after the negative ni; meaning uncertain
amdrom: amdrom (modern form uncertain) — very heavy, heavy; adjective, am- + trwm (trom) 'heavy'; yn amdrom 'heavy', predicative; possibly 'heavy with young' (uncertain)
tebygei: tebygu (tebygu) — to suppose, think, imagine; 3 sg. imperfect 'he thought' (ual y tebygei 'so that he thought'); radical after the particle y
uanec: maneg (maneg) — glove; noun f. (spelt manec); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after y, whether the feminine article or 'his' (yn y uanec 'in his glove')
llinin: llinyn (llinyn) — string, cord, thread; noun m., spelt llinin (ac a llinin 'and with a string'); radical after a 'with'
rwymaw: rhwymo (rhwymo) — to bind, tie; verbal noun, spelt rwymaw; r- writes rh-; the soft mutation (rh>r) after the fronted phrase ac a llinin cannot be told from the spelling
geneu: genau (genau) — mouth, opening; noun m. (geneu y uanec 'the mouth of the glove'); radical, the object of the verbal noun rwymaw
ynyd: yny (hyd oni) — until; yny + yd, the preverbal particle, joined before oed (ynyd oed y crydyon yn dala 'until the shoemakers were holding'); no mutation
blwyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f.; written blwyn, an apparent slip for blwydyn (the Red Book has blwydyn); radical after a 'and' (A blwyn yuelly 'and a year thus')
thra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (A thra geffit y gantaw 'and while there was got from him'); spirant-mutated (t>th) after a 'and'

__broaden__.kyuot: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 2 sg. imperative 'rise!' (kyuot y uynyd ar uyrr 'rise up quickly') · also kyuodi, verbal noun 'rising' in the short form kyuot (yn kyuot yn oreu 'rising best')
__broaden__.uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a · also uy (fy) 'my', with the nasal mutation of d- written as n on the possessive (uyn diua i 'my destruction')
__broaden__.kymry: Kymry (Cymru) — Wales (strictly the Welsh, Cymry, here the country); proper name; the nasal mutation of yg Kymry 'in Wales' (yng Nghymru) is shown only on the preceding yg · also kymryt (cymryd) 'to take', verbal noun written kymry without the t, a scribal slip (kymry llywenyd 'taking joy')
__broaden__.gwyn: Proper name — Gwyn (gwyn also 'white, fair'), father of Heilyn, in Heilyn uab Gwyn Hen 'Heilyn son of Gwyn the Old'; radical after uab · also in Gwyn Gloew, father of Cigfa (uerch Gwyn Gloew 'daughter of Gwyn Gloew'); radical after uerch
__broaden__.traws: traws (traws) — across, athwart, crosswise; noun/adjective in ar traws 'across' (ar traws yr auon 'across the river'); radical after ar · also y traws 'the quarter, the direction' (y traws y managassei ef 'the direction in which he had shown'); exact sense uncertain
__broaden__.uynhaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (na uynhaf 'I do not want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the negative na · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the affirmative particle a (mi a uynhaf 'I will want, I mean to')
__broaden__.uynnu: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; verbal noun, soft-mutated (m>u) after dy 'your' (wrth dy uynnu 'according to your wish') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the preposition y 'to' (y uynnu medi 'to want to reap')
__broaden__.uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after ar 'on' (ar uedwl medi 'on the thought of reaping')
__broaden__.geluydyt: celfyddyd (celfyddyd) — craft, trade, art, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (Pa geluydyt 'what craft') · also soft-mutated (c>g) after the feminine article y (y geluydyt 'the craft')
__broaden__.grydyon: crydd (crydd) — shoemaker; noun m., plural in -yon (modern cryddion); soft-mutated (c>g) after gan 'with, among' (gan grydyon) · also soft-mutated (c>g) after holl 'all' (holl grydyon 'all the shoemakers')
__broaden__.gedymdeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., soft-mutated as object (yn gedymdeith 'as a companion') · also soft after 'y 'his' (a'y gedymdeith 'and his companion') · also soft after dy 'your' (dy gedymdeith 'your companion') and after the linking a in ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'
__broaden__.weleisti: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. preterite weleist with the pronoun ti written on, 'you saw', soft-mutated after a (noc a weleisti 'than what you saw') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) after na (na weleisti gedymdeith 'that you did not see a companion')
__broaden__.greft: crefft (crefft) — craft, trade, skill; noun f.; soft-mutated (c>g) as the direct object directly after the verb (cheisswn greft 'let us seek a craft'); cause the soft mutation of an object after an inflected verb · also soft-mutated (c>g) after pa 'what' (pa greft 'what craft')
__broaden__.dwf: twf (twf) — growth, stature; noun m. (a uei uawr y dwf a'e ueint 'that was big in his growth and his size'); soft-mutated (t>d) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (t>d) after un 'one' (yn un dwf 'in one growth')
__broaden__.benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head') · also soft after a preceding adjective (Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydaut Benn 'the Hospitality of the Head') · also soft-mutated (p>b) after uch 'above' (uch benn llech 'above a slab')
__broaden__.ben: pen (pen) — head; noun m. (ar y ben 'on his head'); soft-mutated (p>b) after the possessive y 'his' · also soft-mutated (p>b) after o 'from' (o ben yr orssed 'from the top of the mound')
__broaden__.lywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (diruawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive y 'his' (a dwyn y lywenyd y gantaw 'and taking his joy from him')
__broaden__.welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort')
__broaden__.weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object of welsynt (y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith 'where they had never seen work'); gweith 'time' is possible but less likely
__broaden__.gyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; 3 sg. preterite, soft-mutated after y (y gyrchwys 'he made for') · also soft-mutated after the relative particle a with the object fronted (y gaer a gyrchwys ef 'the fort he made for')
__broaden__.gyflym: kyflym (cyflym) — swift; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after yn (yn gyflym caeu y got 'quickly shutting the bag') · also soft-mutated (k>g) after y in an adverbial phrase (y gyflym 'quickly')
__broaden__.degach: tec (teg) — fair, pleasant; comparative degach 'pleasanter' (yn degach genthi 'pleasanter to her'); soft-mutated (t>d) after predicative yn · also soft-mutated (t>d) after the noun wenith (wenith degach 'fairer wheat'); cause uncertain
__broaden__.a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
__broaden__.yt: y 'to' — conjugated preposition, 2 sg. 'to you', modern iti, spelt yt beside itt and itti (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'for fear of dishonour to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'; derw yt 'it has befallen you') · also yd 'corn, grain', noun m. (yr yt arall 'the other corn')
__broaden__.gadwn: gadu (gadael) — to let, allow; 1 pl. present 'we allow, will allow' (-wn) (nys gadwn 'we will not allow it'); no mutation (g- radical after ny + 's) · also cadw (cadw) 'to keep', 1 sg. imperfect/conditional 'I would keep' (mi a gadwn gywirdeb 'I would keep faithfulness'), soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
__broaden__.tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud) · also 'beyond', preposition (tra y gefyn 'beyond his back', i.e. back again)
__broaden__.uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great') · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after yn in the adverbial yn uawr 'greatly'
__broaden__.oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best') · also soft-mutated (g lost) after yn (yn oreu yn y byt 'best in the world')
